What I check first in a website audit.

1. Can I tell what you do in 5 seconds?
2. Can I call you in one tap?
3. Does it load fast on a phone?
4. Is there proof, like reviews?

Most sites fail at least one.

Which one do you think yours fails?

Doing free audits for 5 businesses today.

I'll check your website speed, how it works on a phone, and how easy it is to contact you.

No pitch. Just the results and quick fixes.

Drop your website link below to claim one of the 5 spots.

A free audit isn't a sales trick.

It's the fastest way to show you know what you're doing. If the fixes help, people remember who gave them.

Give first. Always.

Would you rather get advice or a pitch?

Audit day. Here's what I look at on every site you send.

Speed on a phone. How easy it is to contact you. Whether the page tells a stranger why to pick you.

Then I send back the quick fixes. No pitch.

Spots are going fast.

Missed the audit spots this morning?

Reply AUDIT and I'll add your site to the list for this week.

AI voice has gotten scary good.

Natural pauses. Real tone. It can handle someone talking over it.

The question isn't whether it sounds human. It's whether it knows your business well enough to help.

Have you heard a good one yet?

"Won't an AI phone agent sound robotic?"

Fair question. Today's voice agents pause naturally, use a voice that fits your brand, and reply without lag.

The easiest way to judge is to call one.

What's your biggest worry about putting AI on your phone line?

An audit finding I see all the time.

The phone number is only in the footer.

Nobody scrolls to the footer to call you. Put it at the top.

Where is your number right now?

A pattern I keep seeing in audits.

Beautiful site. Great photos. Great story. Not one button to book or call.

Pretty doesn't pay. A clear next step does.

Does your site make it obvious what to do?

What's the one question every customer asks before they hire you?

That question belongs on your homepage. Drop it below and I'll show you where it goes.

Chat assistants on websites used to be terrible.

Canned answers. Dead ends. "Please email us."

Now they can answer real questions about your services and book the visit.

Would you add one to your site?

Most people visiting a local business website are on their phone.

If your site looks great on a computer but the mobile menu is clunky and slow, you're losing those visitors, plus any ad money you spent to get them.

Open your site on your phone right now.

Does it load in under 2 seconds? Be honest below.

Common audit finding.

The contact form works, but the emails go to an inbox nobody checks.

Test your own form today. Then check where the message actually lands.

Did it show up?

When we rebuild a site, the first draft is never the design.

It's the path. Where a visitor lands, what they read, where they tap to call.

Get the path right and the design has a job to do.

What's the path on your site?

Still doing free website audits this week.

Drop your link or reply AUDIT. You'll get the top fixes back in plain English, no pitch.

Every lead should get a reply in under a minute, even at midnight.

Not a full answer. Just "Got it, here's what happens next."

That one message keeps them from calling your competitor.

How long does your first reply take?

What a 24/7 lead engine looks like.

1. A visitor lands on your site
2. A chat assistant answers their questions
3. They book a call
4. A reminder text goes out
5. The lead is saved in your CRM

All while you sleep.

Which piece is missing from your setup?

Common audit finding.

5 buttons at the top of the page, all saying different things.

One main action. Call, book or quote. Pick one and make it loud.

How many buttons are at the top of yours?

Our lead engine, honestly.

The site chat answers. The phone line answers. Every lead lands in our CRM, and I get the details right away.

I didn't build it to look cool. I built it because I was losing leads to my own slow replies.

Where are you losing yours?

Which would help your business more this month?

A) More leads
B) Faster replies
C) More reviews
D) A better website

Reply with your letter.

Review requests should go out automatically.

Job done, happy customer, a text an hour later with a link to leave a review.

Most owners forget to ask. Automation doesn't.

How do you ask for reviews now?

Local service businesses don't need flashy effects.

They need a clear way to contact you, fast phone answers, tap to call buttons, and a simple way to collect Google reviews.

That's it. That's the list.

Tag a local business owner who needs to catch more calls.

A pattern I see a lot.

No reviews anywhere on the website, and plenty of great ones sitting on Google.

You already earned the trust. Show it where people decide.

Are your Google reviews on your website?

We made a free kit for home service owners on getting more Google reviews.

Because plenty of owners don't need a new website first. They need 20 more 5 star reviews.

It's free here
evogencyglobal.com/free-review-kit

Last few free audits for this week.

Reply AUDIT or drop your website below.

The apps you already pay for can probably talk to each other.

Your form, your calendar, your CRM, your invoicing. Most of them connect.

Nobody set it up, so your team does the copying.

What do you copy by hand every week?

If your team copies form entries into a spreadsheet and then into a CRM, you're losing hours every week.

And every copy is a chance to get a phone number wrong.

Let your apps pass the data to each other.

Which two apps do you wish talked to each other?

Common audit finding.

The website shows one phone number. Google shows another.

Mismatched info confuses customers and Google both.

Check your number, hours and address everywhere today. All matching?

One thing building our own systems taught me.

The tech is rarely the hard part. Knowing exactly what should happen when a lead comes in is.

Write your process down first. Then automate it.

Is your lead process written down anywhere?

If a new lead texted your business right now, who would see it first?

Reply honestly. Most owners say "me, eventually."

Weekend tip.

Take 5 minutes and Google your own business like a customer would.

What comes up first? Is the info right? Would you call you?

Tell me what you find.

The common thread from this week's website audits.

[FILL IN, how many sites out of how many] had [FILL IN, the most common problem], adding [FILL IN, how much load time] to load times.

Easy fixes. Big impact.

Want us to check your site for the same issues? Drop your link below.

Most website problems I find in audits take under an hour to fix.

Bigger buttons. A clearer headline. Smaller images. The phone number at the top.

Small fixes, more calls.

Which one could you do today?

Next week I'm opening up about how we set up websites and AI receptionists for clients.

What it takes, what changes, and who it's actually right for.

What do you want to know first?

Didn't get an audit this week?

Reply AUDIT and I'll still look at your site. Free.
